recipes.name: Black Bean and Salsa Soup
ingredients_raw: 2 (15 ounce) cans black beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: In an electric food processor or blender, combine beans, broth, salsa, and cumin. Blend until fairly smooth.
Heat the bean mixture in a saucepan over medium heat until thoroughly heated.
Ladle soup into 4 individual bowls, and top each bowl with 1 tablespoon of the sour cream and 1/2 tablespoon green onion.

raw_recipe.headline: Black Bean and Salsa Soup
raw_recipe.description: Black beans, salsa, veggie broth and cumin are tossed into the blender. Transfer to a pot and heat until warm and bubbly. Serve with a dollop of sour cream and a sprinkling of green onion.

review.reviewBody: This is a fantastic recipe! Now know why there are so many glowing reviews. It's so easy (I was done, from start to finish in 15 minutes. We're vegetarian and it's difficult to find a black bean soup in restaurants that's not made with chicken stock or doesn't have bacon. Now I can make the black bean soup that my husband loves so much right at home. Upon other reviewers suggestions, I saved one cup of beans to add whole, I added 3 teaspoons lime juice, triple the cumin, 1 teaspoon garlic, freshly chopped cilantro and 1/2 fresh jalapeno pepper. I also used the immersion blender and blended the soup right in the pot (talk about a great invention!). The soup came out perfect and tasted great with quesadillas. Next time, I'll probably saute some onions and add some corn for a different taste in the soup. Thanks very much for this recipe. It is definitely a keeper!!

MARYANNE'S SHORT PARAGRAPH DESCRIBING THIS SAYS "TAKES ABOUT 5 MINUTES TO PUT TOGETHER" HOWEVER IT ALSO SAYS "10 PREP, 10 COOK, READY IN 20". MISLEADING TO SAY 5 MIN TO PUT TOGETHER (DEPENDS ON WHAT YOUR DEFINITION OF "PUT TOGETHER" MEANS TO YOU). HERE IS A HEALTHIER, MORE SIMPLE WAY TO TO DO THIS. THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IMO IS TO USE ORGANIC INGREDIENTS TO GET THE MOST MACRO/MICRO NUTRIENTS (& YES EVEN THE CUMIN SHOULD BE ORGANIC, THINK COSTCO). IF YOU HAVE A VITAMIX ALL YOU NEED TO DO IS PUT EVERYTHING INSIDE, MINUS THE SOUR CREAM, PUT IT ON SOUP & LET THE VITAMIX DO ALL OF THE WORK, IT'S COMPLETELY COOKED IN LESS THEN 5 MINUTES . BEST PART IS ALL YOU HAVE TO CLEAN IS THE VITAMIX. I DO NOT EAT DAIRY SO I ADD SOME CHOPPED CILANTRO (STEMS INCLUDED FOR EXCELLENT FLAVOR), A DRIZZLE OF ORGANIC WALNUT OR TOASTED SESAME SEED OIL, JUICE FROM HALF A LIME (ADD SOME ZEST IF YOU LIKE SOUR), SOME CHOPPED JALAPENO W/ SEEDS & STEMS IF YOU LIKE SPICY & THE SCALLIONS. I CHOP EVERYTHING WHILE THE VITAMIX IS COOKING THE SOUP. THIS ISN'T THE BEST SOUP IN THE WORLD BUT IF YOU ARE PRESSED FOR TIME IT'S SUPER EASY & HARD TO MESS IT UP. IT'S KIND OF NOISY THOUGH BUT IF YOU DON'T MIND IT THEN IT'S A VERY HEALTHY ALTERNATIVE TO MOST OF THE CANNED JUNK THAT'S ON THE SHELVES AT THE STORE. NOTHING WORSE THEN SOUP THAT TASTES LIKE A CAN.

i was really nervous making this today because I cook for seniors, but wanted to try something different. I did add sauteed onion and garlic, because i always do to my "better than boullion" veg broth. I changed the servings to 30ish which took 14 (all i had) cans of black beans. 10 1/2 cups of broth, 2 tbsp cumin, and only 3 cups of medium salsa. I used my hand blender to blend, leaving a creamy, rustic look, then added corn. My regular taste tester had his thumb up before he even put the spoon down! I'm serving this with cheese quesadillas! Money maker! Thank you for this incredibly easy and adaptable recipe!

So easy and delicious! I sauteed a little minced garlic before adding the rest of the ingredients. I like my soup chunky, so I combined everything in a saucepan and used an immersion blender to give it a little texture. The first time I made it, I added half a can of corn to bulk it up a little for my kiddos. The second time I omitted the corn and it was still so delicious.

If in a hurry I would have made as written but sometimes I like to boost the broth. So I sautéed the 1/2 diced onion, + 1 minced garlic and cumin at the end of sauté. Added 1 quart chicken broth to that along with 1 tsp dried epazote. Simmered for about 20 minutes and then added the beans (used 3 cans) and salsa.

I liked how quick and easy this is to make. It is a great meal with little to no effort. A truly "fast-food" for the home cook. My Blendtec even has a soup setting that heats the soup as it blends! I will make this again and again.

Ha! I thought *I* created this and was searching for a way to submit *my* idea. Then I did a search and found this! I made nearly the same thing but like most, with some alterations. I used one can reduced-sodium black beans (not rinsed), one 14-oz can reduced sodium chicken broth, and one tub of refrigerated salsa (about 16 oz) along with a healthy dose of cumin. The salsa was "medium," so a little too hot for me, but you'd never know the soup was low sodium because it was BIG on flavor. To give it a little body, I smashed some of the beans with a fork before adding them, but other than that, it all went into one sauce pot and just heated through. No prep because with salsa, all the chopping is done. Low-calorie, too. If I did the math right, the whole pot - about 3-4 servings - was 450 calories. A definite make-again choice.

This soup was truly delicious – in my own opinion. My kids found it too spicy, or were afraid to taste it… their loss. I definitely plan to make this again. So fast, so easy, so satisfying! 
I’ve made salsa in the past by cooking diced tomatoes, diced onions, garlic, and a bit of s’chug (super-hot hot pepper mix). So I simply added those ingredients to the soup pot, figuring everything’s anyways cooking together for a bit. Skipped the onions. 
Beans: 1 can (15oz) ‘vegetarian beans’ (i.e. white beans in sweetened tomato sauce + dash of vinegar)
Salsa: ½ can diced tomatoes (i.e. 14 oz)
+ 1 clove garlic (frozen cube)
+ 1/3 tsp s’chug (was too much; max ¼ tsp next time)
Cumin: 1 tsp cumin
Broth: 2 cups veg broth (lightweight vegetable soup, left over from another day)
Other: 1 tsp salt. Also 1-2 tsp olive oil (because my baby, standing on a stepladder, helpfully handed me the bottle, so I thanked him and used a little.)
Brought to a solid boil, then blended thoroughly. Added two handfuls of chopped broccoli (such a great item to have in the freezer) and reheated for just 5 min. Served with a dollop of greek yogurt.

First time I've rated/reviewed! Fastest & yummiest soup you can imagine. I only had refried black beans; guess what--make it even easier--no blender/immersion needed. And to the misanthrope reviewers out there--especially the dummy who blamed the salsa--what made you even THINK the onions could taste cooked?? Then said it tasted good, but rated it one star. I don't get it. Chicken stock, generous w/cumin, onion powder, and garlic pepper. You just won't believe how yummy this is!!!!

I read the recipe and read the reviews. The result is using the published recipe as a guide. What I did based on my reading is the following: 

1) Sauteed 1/3 cup chopped onion and 2 cloves of minced garlic, 1/3 minced jalapeno pepper in 2 tsp olive oil
2) Added 1 1/2 cups low sodium chicken broth and 1 can Rotel Mexican Style tomatoes (with lime and cilantro) in place of salsa

Let mixture simmer for 5 minutes.

3) Added 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp chili powder, 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper to broth

4) Rinsed and drained 1 1/2 cans black beans and added to broth/tomatoes; reserve 1/2 can beans undrained

5) Mix in beans and used immersion blender to break up beans

6) Added 1/2 can whole black beans

7) Let mixture simmer on low heat for 10-15 minutes.

8) Added 1/4 tsp sea salt 

9) Just prior to serving, add 1 T chopped cilantro

This came out very tasty and spicy. If you don't like spicy, omit the jalapeno. It was very easy as well.

Love this easy soup. I used a 29 oz can of black beans, about a cup and half of my own homemade salsa, 2 cups broth and a hefty teaspoon of cumin. Put it all in a pot and used my immersion blending stick to puree it. I added an additional 14 oz can of whole black beans and heated it all up! So good, top with green onions, sour cream, extra salsa, whatever you want.

I used a red bean, chickpea and pea (5:3:2 ratio by drained weight) garlicky hummus with a chunky homemade salsa. Needn't add anything but 2 tablespoons of water. Used homemade Greek yogurt instead of sour cream. Served with warm soda bread. An awesome lunch, we were well satisfied. :)
Thias soup was very good. I followed the recipe exactly. My only tweak was adding shredded Monterey Jack cheese after serving up in bowl.

Good recipe to add what you want, depending on time you have. I sautéed onions and carrots, then added other ingredients plus garlic. Toward end of cooking added a tablespoon balsamic vinegar and frozen corn. Easy and good!
Super easy and delicious!!! I omitted the sour cream and green onions only because I didn't have them on hand at the time.

It was surprisingly delicious! I tried this when I didn't feel like cooking and (honestly) had low expectations, given the simplicity. However, I enjoyed it very much. It was tasty and satisfying. I'll be making it again, for sure!
No changes!!!!! Don’t do it!!! You don’t need to!!!!
Lightning quick and very tasty. Whole family really enjoyed it. A literal 15 minute (or less) win. Thanks so much!
I loved this. The flavors were perfect imo and it came together so fast
